title: Making Friends in a New City
summary: Ama and Carlos share honest ideas for meeting people after moving to a new place.

cover.scene: Flat 2D illustration: Ama and Carlos on a park bench with takeaway cups, a city skyline and trees behind them, no text

sentences.text: Hello, and welcome back! Today we are talking about moving to a new city.
I know this feeling well. When I moved here, I did not know anyone.
How did you feel in the first weeks?
Honestly, I felt lonely. I spent most evenings alone in my flat.
I felt the same when I changed cities for my job.
What was the hardest part for you?
Starting conversations. I was afraid that people would think I was strange.
But most people are friendly, and many of them are new here too.
That is true. After a while, I realised that I was not the only one.
So the first step is to be brave and say hello.

quiz.q: How did Carlos feel at first?
What was the hardest part for him?

quiz.explain: So the first step is to be brave and say hello.

sentences.text: So, Ama, what really worked for you?
I joined a weekly running club, and that changed everything.
Why was it so useful?
You already have something in common, so it is easy to talk.
I tried a language exchange, and I made two good friends there.
I also said yes to every invitation, even when I felt tired.
That is a great rule. Small plans can turn into real friendships.
And do not forget your neighbours. A simple smile in the lift helps.
Yes, and be patient. Good friends take time.
Thanks for listening, everyone, and see you next week!

quiz.explain: I joined a weekly running club.
I tried a language exchange, and I made two good friends there.
Be patient. Good friends take time.
